lesson.title: Build a Custom ls CLI Tool in Rust
lesson.goal: build a command-line tool in Rust with cargo that parses arguments

sources.title: Build a Custom ls CLI Tool in Rust

steps.title: Create project and add clap
steps.instructions: Run cargo new bestls && cd bestls. Add clap with the derive feature under [dependencies] in Cargo.toml.

targets.caption: Add clap dependency with derive feature

hints: Initialize a new Rust binary project with cargo new.
Open Cargo.toml and locate the [dependencies] section.
Add clap = { version = "4.5.39", features = ["derive"] } under [dependencies].
common_mistakes: Forgetting features = ["derive"] on clap, which prevents #[derive(Parser)] from compiling.
Running cargo commands from the parent folder instead of inside bestls.

steps.title: Define CLI struct and parse arguments
steps.instructions: In src/main.rs define a struct deriving Parser with an optional PathBuf field and call parse() in main. Run cargo run -- -h.

explanations.topic: Passing flags to cargo run using --
Auto-generated help output from clap Parser

hints: Import clap::Parser and std::path::PathBuf at the top of src/main.rs.
Annotate struct CLI with #[derive(Debug, Parser)] and add path: Option<PathBuf>.
Pass -h after -- when running cargo run so it reaches your binary.
common_mistakes: Passing -h directly to cargo run instead of after --.
Forgetting to import std::path::PathBuf or clap::Parser.
steps.code: use clap::Parser; use std::path::PathBuf; #[derive(Debug, Parser)] struct CLI { path: Option<PathBuf>, } fn main() { let cli = CLI::parse(); println!("Hello, world!"); }

steps.title: Add command metadata and default path
steps.instructions: Add #[command(version, about, long_about = ...)] to the struct, default the path to "." with unwrap_or, and print it. Run cargo run -- longpath.

targets.caption: Provide a default path of current directory

explanations.topic: Using command attribute for version and long_about

hints: Add #[command(version, about, long_about = "Best Ls command ever")] above struct CLI.
Use cli.path.unwrap_or(PathBuf::from(".")) to fall back to the current directory.
Print the path using println!("{}", path.display()).
common_mistakes: Trying to print PathBuf directly without calling .display().
steps.code: #[command(version, about, long_about = "Best Ls command ever")] struct CLI { path: Option<PathBuf>, } let path = cli.path.unwrap_or(PathBuf::from(".")); println!("{}", path.display());

steps.title: Validate path existence with colored output
steps.instructions: Add owo-colors to Cargo.toml and check fs::exists(&path) in main in src/main.rs. Print a red error when the path is missing or unreadable, then run the binary with a bogus path.

targets.caption: Verify whether the target path exists
Red error for a missing path

hints: Add owo-colors = "4.2.1" to Cargo.toml and import owo_colors::OwoColorize.
Import std::fs and match on if let Ok(does_exist) = fs::exists(&path).
Call .red() on the error string literal inside println!.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to import owo_colors::OwoColorize, which provides the .red() trait method.
Treating fs::exists(&path) as a bool instead of unwrapping its Result with if let Ok(...).
steps.code: if let Ok(does_exist) = fs::exists(&path) { if does_exist { } else { println!("{}", "Path does not exist".red()); } } else { println!("{}", "error reading directory".red()); }

steps.title: Read directory entries into a vector
steps.instructions: Write get_files(path: &Path) -> Vec<String> using fs::read_dir and print each name in main. Run cargo run.
hints: Import std::path::Path and define fn get_files(path: &Path) -> Vec<String>.
Iterate over fs::read_dir(path) and extract each entry's file_name().
Convert the OsString via .into_string().unwrap_or("unknown name".into()) and push it to data.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to pass &path to get_files(&path) in main.
Not handling the Result from into_string() on OsString.
steps.code: fn get_files(path: &Path) -> Vec<String> { let mut data = Vec::default(); if let Ok(read_dir) = fs::read_dir(path) { for entry in read_dir { if let Ok(file) = entry { data.push(file.file_name().into_string().unwrap_or("unknown name".into())); } } } data }

steps.title: Extract metadata into FileEntry struct
steps.instructions: Add strum and strum_macros, define EntryType and FileEntry, and fill metadata via fs::metadata in map_data. Run cargo run.

targets.caption: Define EntryType enum and FileEntry struct

explanations.topic: Using strum Display macro on enums

hints: Add strum = { version = "0.27", features = ["derive"] } and strum_macros = "0.27" to Cargo.toml.
Call fs::metadata(&file.path()), not &path, so each entry gets its own metadata.
Use meta.is_dir() and meta.len() to populate e_type and len_btyes.
common_mistakes: Passing &path instead of &file.path() to fs::metadata, causing every entry to show the directory's metadata.
Forgetting to change get_files return type from Vec<String> to Vec<FileEntry>.
steps.code: #[derive(Debug, Display)] enum EntryType { File, Dir, } #[derive(Debug)] struct FileEntry { name: String, e_type: EntryType, len_btyes: u64, modified: String, } fn map_data(file: fs::DirEntry, data: &mut Vec<FileEntry>) { if let Ok(meta) = fs::metadata(&file.path()) { data.push(FileEntry { name: file.file_name().into_string().unwrap_or("unknown name".into()), e_type: if meta.is_dir() { EntryType::Dir } else { EntryType::File }, len_btyes: meta.len(), modified: "".to_string(), }); } }

steps.title: Format and color output with tabled
steps.instructions: Add tabled, derive Tabled with rename attributes on FileEntry, and print a Table styled with Style::rounded(). Run cargo run.

targets.caption: Create and style the output table

hints: Add tabled = "0.20.0" to Cargo.toml and import Table, Style, Color, Columns, Rows from tabled.
Add #[derive(Debug, Tabled)] and #[tabled(rename = "...")] attributes on FileEntry fields.
Use table.with(Style::rounded()) and table.modify(...) before println!("{}", table).
common_mistakes: Importing Style from owo_colors or clap instead of tabled::settings::Style.
Forgetting mut on let mut table = Table::new(...) before calling .with() and .modify().
steps.code: #[derive(Debug, Tabled)] struct FileEntry { #[tabled(rename = "Name")] name: String, #[tabled(rename = "Type")] e_type: EntryType, #[tabled(rename = "Size B")] len_btyes: u64, modified: String, } let mut table = Table::new(get_files(&path)); table.with(Style::rounded()); table.modify(Columns::first(), Color::FG_BRIGHT_CYAN); table.modify(Columns::one(2), Color::FG_BRIGHT_MAGENTA); table.modify(Columns::one(3), Color::FG_BRIGHT_MAGENTA); table.modify(Rows::first(), Color::FG_BRIGHT_GREEN); println!("{}", table);

steps.title: Format modification dates with chrono
steps.instructions: Add chrono and convert meta.modified() into DateTime<Utc> in map_data. Run cargo run -- src.

targets.caption: Format file modification timestamp with chrono

hints: Add chrono = "0.4.41" to Cargo.toml and import chrono::{DateTime, Utc}.
Convert modi (SystemTime) via let date: DateTime<Utc> = modi.into();.
Format the date using date.format("%a %b %e %Y") and return String::default() in the else branch.
common_mistakes: Naming the variable mod instead of modi, since mod is a reserved Rust keyword.
Forgetting the type annotation DateTime<Utc> on the .into() conversion.
steps.code: modified: if let Ok(modi) = meta.modified() { let date: DateTime<Utc> = modi.into(); format!("{}", date.format("%a %b %e %Y")) } else { String::default() }

steps.title: Add JSON output flag with serde
steps.instructions: Add serde (with derive) and serde_json to Cargo.toml, derive Serialize on your entry structs, and add a #[arg(short, long)] json: bool flag to the CLI struct. When cli.json is true, print serde_json::to_string of the files, then run cargo run -- -j.

targets.caption: Serialize entries to JSON when -j is passed

hints: Add serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] } and serde_json = "1.0" to Cargo.toml.
Derive Serialize on both EntryType and FileEntry.
Add #[arg(short, long)] json: bool to CLI and branch on cli.json in main.
common_mistakes: Deriving Serialize on FileEntry without also deriving Serialize on EntryType.
Forgetting #[arg(short, long)] on json: bool, which makes clap treat it as a positional argument and panic.
steps.code: #[arg(short, long)] json: bool, } if cli.json { println!("{}", serde_json::to_string(&get_files(&path)).unwrap_or("cannot parse json".to_string())); } else { print_table(&path); }
